scope: Private research comparison of frozen original K1 against small and wave variants; not a fixed-v1 capsule benchmark or provider qualification.

baseline.label: original-k1
baseline.description: Frozen original K1 shared-memory argmax; 256 threads per row. Baseline is measured separately against each candidate.

small.description: Shared-memory reduction using 32 threads for columns <= 32, otherwise 256.

wave.description: 256 threads per row; width-32 wave shuffles, eight shared partial results, then wave 0 reduction. Requires warp size 32.

build.note: Compile phase used loader diagnostics and required no GPU lease; measured runs disabled diagnostics.

analysis.sample_units: microseconds per launch; each raw sample is HIP event elapsed time for a batch of 100 launches divided by 100
analysis.median_definition: Arithmetic mean of sorted samples at zero-based positions 9 and 10, separately for each provider, candidate pairing, shape and trial.
analysis.ratio_definition: baseline_median_us / candidate_median_us; greater than 1 means a lower candidate median. Ratio of medians, not median of paired ratios.
verification: All compile and run receipt output byte counts and SHA-256 hashes verified against evidence files.
All three phases process-complete with return code 0 and no process failure; actual prefix evidence hashes match before/after and receipts report physical and semantic equality.
Both measured runs diagnostic=false, empty stderr, preflight passed, exclusive GPU lease held through phase receipt and released with matching phase SHA-256.
Executable identical across both trials, matching compile output; comparator and variants header match reviewed hashes, original K1 header matches first comparison compile.
Both providers passed CPU bit-value/index validation before and after timing in every case.
All 960 raw samples finite and positive; all 48 medians recomputed exactly and 24 baseline/candidate ratios calculated separately.
Shape, seed and input digest match across trials, across candidate pairings, and the original K1 comparison inputs.
Device identity, HIP versions and complete loader path list match across trials; loader path list matches prior K1 run.
limitations: Only six K=1 shapes and one deterministic distinct finite F32 input per shape on one gfx1151 device; no ties, NaNs or general-K qualification.
Two trials remain separate with no pooling, confidence intervals, statistical significance or broad workload claims.
Small wave timing differences are descriptive observations; these two trials do not establish a repeatable or statistically significant speedup.
Small is tested first, then wave; fresh paired baselines reduce reliance on cross-candidate comparisons, but run order and system drift remain possible influences.
HIP event batch timings include provider stream work and possible host enqueue gaps; they are not pure kernel latency. Input transfer, CPU validation, allocation and event creation are excluded.
The baseline here is original K1, not the bitonic adapter from the first comparison. No rocPRIM or separate control comparison was measured.
Loaded paths are observations; metadata coverage remains unknown and vendor authenticity unverified.
External host/library hash snapshot checks reported by the root reviewer are not independently certified by this artifact; phase output files and loader path observations were independently checked.
Receipt hashes identify external evidence. Large prefix evidence files, executable and library contents are not embedded in this portable artifact.

measurement.comparison_order: small then wave; six shapes per candidate; baseline measured separately for each candidate
measurement.scope: private-research-only; not fixed-v1 or provider qualification
measurement.semantics: K=1 original column index of maximum value, finite F32 distinct values per row; CPU bit-value/index oracle; no tie/NaN/general-K qualification
measurement.timing_scope: HIP event batch elapsed / 100; all provider stream work including possible host enqueue gaps; excludes input transfer, validation, allocation, event creation
